title: Dendrite area improved response-time predictions in 158 selected Allen human cells
abstract: We tested whether reconstructed dendrite surface area improves a prediction of membrane response time after input resistance and cell labels are known. We used linked Allen Cell Types measurements and held out whole donors. mouse: 509 cells from 372 donors; squared log error fell from 0.08450 to 0.07843. Gain was 0.00607, with a 97.5% donor interval of -0.00037 to 0.01227. The relative gain was 7.18%. human: 158 cells from 35 donors; squared log error fell from 0.16986 to 0.12532. Gain was 0.04454, with a 97.5% donor interval of 0.02185 to 0.06977. The relative gain was 26.22%. Intervals condition on fitted predictions. These data test prediction in selected brain slices. They do not measure specific membrane capacitance or establish a causal effect. Cut dendrites, radius errors, active currents, and selected human donors limit the result.

display.caption: Left: area and an apparent capacitance proxy; this is not a direct capacitance measurement. Right: prediction gain from added surface area, with conditional 97.5% donor intervals. Positive gain means lower error. Only penalty 10 in the full samples is primary.

citations.reason: Mouse source study and prior joint morphology and electrical classification.
Human cell diversity context; the present sample is the older Cell Types API cache, not a new Patch-seq extraction.
Prior model fits and patch measurements of human specific membrane capacitance; our scalar prediction test does not measure that parameter.
Definitions of input resistance and fitted membrane response time.
Prior campaign work shows that prediction gains can depend on model shrinkage. We test cell morphology with different data and no reused code.
The shared dataset README identifies this earlier study of human and mouse specific membrane capacitance. We used its documented raw cache, not its results; its full text was not reviewed.
